items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: A few weeks after I started with Johnny, he hired a trombone player named Herb Gregory... Ted and I shared our bottle with him... After a few months with Johnny Monnegue I left

ctx.x: Sometime later a fellow came to Cincinnati from Kentucky who's name was Zack White. His name was really Zacharias White and he played banjo. There was also a pianist named Johnny Johnson that I had heard when I was living on Kenyon Avenue. Johnny Johnson also played piano by ear and he was well known in the higher society negro class.

One day Zack and Johnny came to my house and told me that there was a fellow in town from Michigan that wanted some musicians to play week-ends at a vacation camp not far from Kalamazoo, and they asked me if I would like to be a part of the group. I had never been more than a hundred miles from Cincinnati and this proposition sounded great to me. Zack and Johnny did not have to ask me twice if I wanted to go with them.

A few days later, we left Cincinnati with this fellow who was older than we were and he was the drummer. We were also joined by a young alto player from Wyoming, Ohio named Jimmie Smith. Jimmie was the second negro that looked like a white boy that I had come in contact with. I had gone south from Cincinnati but now I was going north.
